prompt: On the unit circle, what is the $y$-coordinate of the point at $90^\circ$? (This value is $\sin 90^\circ$.)
hint: $90^\circ$ is a quarter turn, which lands on the positive $y$-axis.

hints.text: $90^\circ$ is a quarter turn, which lands on the positive $y$-axis.
The circle has radius 1, so that top point is $(0, 1)$.

explanation: A quarter turn from the positive $x$-axis lands straight up on the positive $y$-axis.
Since the radius is 1, that point is exactly $(0, 1)$.
Sine is the $y$-coordinate, so $\sin 90^\circ = 1$ — the largest value sine ever reaches.

alternativeExplanations.title: The ceiling of sine
steps: Every point on the unit circle is 1 unit from the center, so no point can be higher than 1.
The top of the circle, at $90^\circ$, is where sine hits that ceiling.
